variants.description: Use 'not (total != expected)' instead of == to compare two floats — logically equivalent but still relies on != for floats.
Introduce a brand-new module src/refunds.py with 'return refunded == original' — same mistake in a previously clean file.
Store the arithmetic result in a local variable 'difference = paid - owed' then compare 'difference == 0.0' — the == is one step removed from the call site.
Use 'abs(computed_tax - expected_tax) == 0' — looks like a tolerance check but uses == 0 with no epsilon, reproducing the same precision failure.
Compare a float to the integer literal 0 instead of 0.0: 'return price == 0' — same mistake, different literal type.
Introduce a private helper '_floats_equal(a, b): return a == b' and call it — the bug is hidden one call-level deeper.
